change_details.before: Primary source reviewed; independent build/run not performed
change_details.after: The current source reports 283/283 DOS entry roles (100%), 174/336 Windows roles and 55/80 Mac jump-table roles with lossless byte coverage; CD-i reconstruction was removed from the current tree and full gameplay/platform equivalence remains unverified.

change_details.after: Scoped PC-98 reconstruction now accepts 33 OP extents / 32 procedures / 4,370 owned bytes, including 487 initialized DATA bytes with actual-consumer and mutation contracts; whole-product source/link ownership remains open.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.after: Incremental DOS C reconstruction still reports 286 strict routines among 331 identities; its native boundary audit now requires exact intermediate FLAGS witnesses and independently rejects a wrong-CS and ADD-assignment mutant without establishing whole-game completion.

events.title: Project metadata updated

before.name: Tang Nano 20K SMD variant
before.notes: Upstream's measured fast20 configuration with SMD and tape reader uses 89% logic and 45 of 46 BSRAM blocks, routes successfully, and boots SINTRAN from 21540& in 26 seconds. This is a verified board/build combination, not a minimum FPGA or memory requirement.

before.name: Tang Nano 20K Winchester default
before.notes: Upstream reports the default Winchester plus tape-reader build at 87% logic and 45 of 46 BSRAM blocks, routed and booting SINTRAN from 20500&. SMD and Winchester together do not route on the tested Tang configuration.

after.name: Tang Nano 20K SMD variant
after.notes: Upstream's measured fast20 configuration with SMD and tape reader uses 89% logic and 45 of 46 BSRAM blocks, routes successfully, and boots SINTRAN from 21540& in 26 seconds. This is a verified board/build combination, not a minimum FPGA or memory requirement.

evidence.excerpt: SMD + tape reader ... routed; 21540& boots SINTRAN in 26 s

after.name: Tang Nano 20K Winchester default
after.notes: Upstream reports the default Winchester plus tape-reader build at 87% logic and 45 of 46 BSRAM blocks, routed and booting SINTRAN from 20500&. SMD and Winchester together do not route on the tested Tang configuration.

evidence.excerpt: Winchester + tape reader (the default) ... routed; 20500& boots SINTRAN

after.name: MEGA65 R6 OPCOM bring-up
after.notes: Upstream reports the R6 whole-machine core running on a tester's physical MEGA65: a 20 MHz ND-120 configuration with 4 MB configured main memory boots to OPCOM and drives the native 640x480 console. SINTRAN was not yet tried on this board, R3 was not run, and the configuration is not claimed as a minimum.

evidence.excerpt: R6 boots to OPCOM on a tester's machine ... 20 MHz ... 4 MB ... R3 not yet run

change_details.before: Reconstructed ND-120 Verilog system with measured FPGA bring-up: tested Tang Nano 20K SMD-only and Winchester variants boot SINTRAN, while combined SMD+Winchester routing fails on Tang; Nexys and MEGA65 work continue.
change_details.after: Reconstructed ND-120 Verilog system with measured Tang Nano boot profiles and physical MEGA65 R6 bring-up to OPCOM; fresh-clone Nexys DDR2 and nested MEGA65 submodule build gaps are also corrected, while R3 hardware and MEGA65 SINTRAN remain untested.

events.title: Stage 1's rooms are packages, and every actor they spawn is named through a binding: the other 20 rooms load into the room slot and require gameplay and the Akropolis stage overlay; 17 of them bind the packages their resources spawn (71 bindings with the square's), and 50 more packages export the task tables those name, by the names the room links already used (61 tables in 51 packages; the rat and moth, the officers, the departure, the security monitors and the three sucklerceph and skull stalker packages export one per role). All 95 resource entries that point outside their room now name <binding>.<export> instead of an address (the square's grinning_stranger.task_desc is grinning_stranger.tasks, like the rest); six whose own file is a texture or not on the disc spawn from a package another entry loads, and resolve to the one export of any binding at that address. The build writes build/exports/<room>.txt, each export a room's data references at its package's slot address, and adds it to that room's undefined symbols (a split input); a symbol two bindings give different addresses is an error. package.slot_of finds an actor package in a variant entry's slots too

events.title: A replay of a rebuild with a loader starts the rebuild in the phase of the original at the entry: the replay core holds the rebuild on its first fetch at the entry until the raster beam is where the original had it, and gives it the CIA timers and the interrupt state of the original there (c64run protocol 7, align), as that phase depends on how the original started and a loader can only set the one of the capture; a program that starts its CIA timers without a force load, as Barbarian does, no longer drifts to a false FAIL

events.title: I fixed the MZ-800 state right after a reset. The emulator put the GDG into MZ-700 mode (DMD 08h) and did not map VRAM at 8000h. On the real machine, after power on and after RESET the GDG is in MZ-800 mode (DMD 0, 320x200) and the memory map is the same as after OUT E4h: ROM at 0000h, CG-ROM at 1000h, VRAM at 8000h-9FFFh, ROM at E000h, RAM elsewhere. MZ-700 mode is switched on later by the ROM (OUT CEh with 08h at E816h). This is shown in the MZ-800 Service Manual (pages 6 and 7), and a simulation of the GDG gate-level netlist gives the same map after a cold and a warm reset.

The flames draw named cells of the landing pad's sparks page, now declared: flame_*, tongue_*, burning_* and smudge_* (30 cells), with 21 palettes the extractor called unread - smudge on row 270 and the twenty fire palettes on row 271 the tongues and burning flames step through - as its variants; the effect tasks are named for their effects (GolemFlameTask, FlameTongueTask, FlameSpriteTask, GunfireParticleTask, MuzzleFlashTask, ExplosionFireballTask, ImpactBurstTask; were ..Task45, ..4C, ..52, ..59, ..44, ..184, ..185), effect 0x4C is EFFECT_NO9_FLAME_TONGUE, and the gunfire smudge is documented as subtractive (was 'additive'). events.title: Every dialogue on the disc decodes (166 of 166): the pipeline follows the second layout tool the game also reads. A decoded dialogue's atlas can state its face (the new bold face dialogue/font_bold), its first_glyph (that tool numbers glyph cells from 0 and has no speaker plates: a title is the glyph cell it draws), and its marks (the ▼ at (242, 242) no cell reaches); MIST room 21's bold glyphs are in cap_glyphs.tsv. Dryfield r04's cells slice across a Japanese page laid out for other text, as the game draws them: they are kept as stored_cells, the text refers to them by cell, and the page is an image of its own (dryfield_r04_glyph_page). change_details.before: MegaST — Atari ST/STE MiSTery-derived FPGA core for MEGA65
change_details.after: MegaST — Atari ST/STe and Falcon030 FPGA core for MEGA65

before.name: MegaST v1.1 on MEGA65 R6
before.notes: Primary README reports stable real-hardware R6 operation with floppy/hard-disk images, TOS 1.04, named games and additional tester-reported TOS/game configurations. Requires an SD card, tos.img and user media. No 45GS02 requirement or guest ST-RAM size is treated as a host CPU/RAM minimum. v1.1 additionally verifies the read-only internal 3.5-inch drive with an original Jim Power disk.

before.name: MegaST v1.0 on MEGA65 R3/R3A
before.notes: The dedicated R3/R3A core keeps 512 KiB of guest ST RAM in FPGA block RAM because HyperRAM is too slow for cycle-exact timing. Upstream reports R3A operation including hard-disk images. Viking and STEroids modes are unavailable. The 512 KiB value is guest configuration, not host minimum RAM.

after.name: MegaST v1.1 on MEGA65 R6
after.notes: Primary README reports stable real-hardware R6 operation with floppy/hard-disk images, TOS 1.04, named games and additional tester-reported TOS/game configurations. Requires an SD card, tos.img and user media. No 45GS02 requirement or guest ST-RAM size is treated as a host CPU/RAM minimum. v1.1 additionally verifies the read-only internal 3.5-inch drive with an original Jim Power disk.

after.name: MegaST v1.0 on MEGA65 R3/R3A
after.notes: The dedicated R3/R3A core keeps 512 KiB of guest ST RAM in FPGA block RAM because HyperRAM is too slow for cycle-exact timing. Upstream reports R3A operation including hard-disk images. Viking and STEroids modes are unavailable. The 512 KiB value is guest configuration, not host minimum RAM.

after.name: MegaST v1.1.6 Falcon030 test on MEGA65 R6
after.min_cpu: 68030 at 16 MHz guest core; optional 32 MHz turbo
after.os: 512 KiB Falcon EmuTOS or Atari TOS 4.0x; tosfalc.img and fcnvram on SD card
after.notes: Falcon030 is an R6-only test variant. Upstream reports EmuTOS, TOS 4.04, several demos/programs and FreeMiNT 1.19 through text shell/TOS desktop; XaAES remains a white screen. The 4 MiB figure is the lowest explicit guest ST-RAM option, not host RAM.

change_details.before: v1.1 stable; R6 internal 3.5-inch drive support verified read-only; R4/R5 remain untested
change_details.after: v1.1.6 adds a test Atari Falcon030 variant for MEGA65 R6; EmuTOS, TOS 4.04, several demos and FreeMiNT boot, while XaAES and multiple Falcon peripherals remain unverified.

change_details.after: Incremental DOS C reconstruction reports 286 strict routines and 331 identities; a new fixup-backed far-call enumerator supports bounded overlay-stub identity arguments without establishing whole-game completion or playability.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: active; shared Amiga palette-slot correctness and independently verified sliced-dither tuning
change_details.after: Development head adds Smooth dithering for one-palette Amiga bitplane modes using per-pixel colour-pair coverage planning and multi-scale interleaved error refinement.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.after: Active NES 6502 static recompiler; native-safe data restoration now protects bytes used by compiled mappings, and bank-qualified cheat reads bind physical PRG offsets and original values.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Active Sharp MZ emulator/debugger; MCP breakpoint names now persist, ignored DD/FD prefixes are modeled explicitly, and MZF size checks handle unreadable files

events.title: Project metadata updated

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Source inspected; no independent build or execution
change_details.after: Source reconstruction reports 30,108 of 30,875 functions identified (97.52%), 88.6% code bytes matched and 87.3% clean source; no independent build or playable result is established.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: Active; 6502 keyed-linear-search dispatch recovery now accepts coherent X- or Y-index loops and rejects mixed-register cases, with unit/build checks and a 35-ROM NES corpus gate reported passing
change_details.after: Development head adds an opt-in, one-shot Retro Skip Idiom analyzer that shares 6502 repair logic, applies strong/referenced candidates and bookmarks unapplied candidates for review.

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.after: Active floppy flux imaging and analysis suite; the Java pipeline now reads A2R 3.x structures and writes A2R v3 raw captures at a default 62.5 ns resolution.

before.name: 512K Lite-client integration
before.os: System 6 with LocalTalk and a MacIP gateway

after.name: 512K Lite-client integration
after.os: System 6 with 128K ROM or later, LocalTalk and a MacIP gateway
after.notes: The v0.1.0 release packages five tools, the TalkIP Driver and AppleTalk On as an 800K HFS disk and StuffIt 1.5 archive. Primary documentation states a Macintosh with 128K ROM or later and 512 KiB RAM, but no minimum CPU is inferred from the machine family.

change_details.before: active; documented Geomys Lite and Flynn Lite 512K integrations
change_details.after: v0.1.0 released: packaged 512K System 6 TCP/IP tools and MacTCP-compatible driver for LocalTalk/MacIP, without MacTCP

events.title: Project metadata updated

change_details.before: General PS1 emulator/debugger and development tooling derived from PCSX. Inspected debugger implementation; classify as reusable tooling, not a game-specific emulation port.
change_details.after: Active PS1 emulator/debugger: current source adds tested NTSC 480i DFE row suppression, SPU-mix WAV capture, safer legacy save-state GPU restoration and correct Lua breakpoint labels; independently unbuilt and unrun

events.title: Project metadata updated

before.name: Dot Chase: selected classic 68k build
before.notes: -m68020 build with intuition.library and graphics.library v39, four-plane LORES screen. No PPC branch is evidenced. RAM and chipset minima are unstated; not independently run.

before.name: Fractalus and Void Trader: selected classic AGA builds
before.notes: Both selected builds use -m68020, explicit AGA 320x256x8bpp and v39 OS libraries. No minimum RAM or measured performance threshold is established. 64 KiB stack requests are not RAM minima.

before.name: Fractalus and Void Trader: PPC OS4 variants
before.notes: ARCH=ppc selects -mcpu=440 and newlib with sam460ex/QEMU intent. The PPC variants use silent audio stubs; Fractalus uses graphics.library fallback rendering. Pacing/freezing limitations are author-reported. This does not cover Dot Chase or the whole collection; exact CPU/RAM minimum remains unverified.

before.name: Planet Chomp, Rolling Steel and Spectral Keep: PPC OS4 source ports
before.notes: The three source-level ports are PPC-only and build with ppc-amigaos-gcc -mcpu=440fp/newlib. Planet Chomp and Rolling Steel use OSMesa 7.8.2 software rendering; Spectral Keep renders its precomputed sprites in software. Upstream reports QEMU sam460ex performance, but no minimum physical CPU or RAM requirement is established.

after.name: Dot Chase: selected classic 68k build
after.notes: -m68020 build with intuition.library and graphics.library v39, four-plane LORES screen. No PPC branch is evidenced. RAM and chipset minima are unstated; not independently run.

after.name: Fractalus and Void Trader: selected classic AGA builds
after.notes: Both selected builds use -m68020, explicit AGA 320x256x8bpp and v39 OS libraries. No minimum RAM or measured performance threshold is established. 64 KiB stack requests are not RAM minima.

after.name: Fractalus and Void Trader: PPC OS4 variants
after.notes: ARCH=ppc selects -mcpu=440 and newlib with sam460ex/QEMU intent. The PPC variants use silent audio stubs; Fractalus uses graphics.library fallback rendering. Pacing/freezing limitations are author-reported. This does not cover Dot Chase or the whole collection; exact CPU/RAM minimum remains unverified.

after.name: Planet Chomp, Rolling Steel and Spectral Keep: PPC OS4 source ports
after.notes: The three source-level ports are PPC-only and build with ppc-amigaos-gcc -mcpu=440fp/newlib. Planet Chomp and Rolling Steel use OSMesa 7.8.2 software rendering; Spectral Keep renders its precomputed sprites in software. Upstream reports QEMU sam460ex performance, but no minimum physical CPU or RAM requirement is established.

after.name: Terra Strike: classic 68k AGA build
after.notes: The primary README explicitly states 68020+, AGA and AmigaOS 3.0+ for the classic build. No minimum RAM is stated; the tracker did not run it.

after.name: Terra Strike: PowerPC AmigaOS 4.1 build
after.notes: ARCH=ppc produces terra_strike_os4 with windowed/full-screen graphics and AHI audio. No physical PowerPC model or RAM minimum is stated.

change_details.before: Six substantive game anchors reviewed across classic 68k and PPC AmigaOS variants; independently unbuilt
change_details.after: Seven substantive original/homebrew game anchors reviewed across classic 68k and PowerPC AmigaOS variants; Terra Strike now has a shared-gameplay AmigaOS 4.1 port; independently unbuilt

events.title: Project metadata updated

after.name: Flynn 512Ke edition
after.notes: Published minimal-plus-Finger edition for a Macintosh 512Ke over LocalTalk, linked with talkip. Requires AppleTalk and a MacIP gateway; no MacTCP or networking INIT. The paired talkip release documentation states 128K ROM or later. No minimum CPU is inferred from the machine name.

change_details.before: Primary source reviewed; independent build/run not performed
change_details.after: v1.13.2 adds a published Flynn 512Ke Telnet/Finger edition using talkip over LocalTalk without MacTCP or a networking INIT; independently unbuilt and unrun

The walk follows a script's operands to its payloads by opcode and message; the record states scripts and the payloads code uses directly as entry points (scripts, animations, transforms, actor_commands, ...). events.title: The Akropolis stage's rooms are declared and their data is room assets: every folder of stage 1 (Akropolis and the MIST) is a group under rooms/akropolis or rooms/mist with its chunks named by role (package, bundle, view<N>_background/_image/_palette, sounds_<k>, dialogue_<k>), shared chunks hoisted to rooms/akropolis; the view sprite sheets are 252 page textures and the effect, model, glyph and panorama pages 44 more, placed in new and widened VRAM regions; all 40 room sound banks name their slots; 17 room models and 70 room clips in 15 banks are converted. Each room package is a `room` asset (tools/peassets/room): the extractor walks it from the stage overlay's per-area tables (indexed by area), gameplay's area table and the record's entry points by role (markers, view masks, samples, area updates, vibration scripts, spare sprite batches, alternate light sets and grids, action triggers), decoding every object in the bytes into <group>/room.toml, which encodes back exactly; types follow from roles and the fields that reach them. The build writes one include per module (header, geometry, view boundaries, action triggers, occluders, cameras, sprites, lights, ambient, placements, surfaces, updates, vibrations, markers, view masks, samples) and the declarations (gen_room_inc.py), which the rooms' C includes where each module's block sits; the rooms' C keeps code, code tables, one-off globals and tuning tables, now without const or section attributes on data. The cafeteria's spot-light storage is fifteen spot lights; the stage maps name the per-area tables of all five stages

events.title: c64-disk: sectors writes the 256 bytes of the given sectors, then with --unreferenced each used sector that no file holds, into one file and gives the track, sector and offset of each; before, bam listed the unreferenced sectors but nothing read their bytes, and bam now names this command as its nextAction when such sectors exist
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: c64-testing: a record file can say where the coverage of the recording starts, with "coverage": "input" (the default, at the first input read of code in RAM), "start" (when the program starts) or a $ address (at its first execution, also at the pc of a registers step), and the record summary gives coverageFrom with the frame and pc where the map starts, or null, because a map that started after the start-up code made an agent think that game_start and its writes did not run; c64run protocol 3 adds coverage on-pc and coverage status
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: An analyzer reference from a data region of the user, the LLM or a heuristic is false code from packed bytes that the analyzer decoded: the import drops it and counts it in references.inData, the analyzer's own reference from there closes also in a run that is not complete, and a classify of data closes the analyzer references from its range; dual-use bytes keep theirs; before, such references stayed in reference pages and reachability and came back on each run
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: A trace of thousands of hits reaches the caller: the hits go as an attachment of the reply, not in the one message that holds at most 1 MiB, and a result too large for one reply gets limit-exceeded with its size and a remedy and a host log line, not a generic operation-failed; hello and ready also carry the package version, so a client and a host of different releases refuse the handshake and name the older side (a development checkout passes against any release), the protocol version is 5, and after a lost session the MCP server gives that refusal instead of the stored machine-state-lost notice
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: c64-source: a read or a write in the I/O area names the register also where the image holds RAM there (lda CI2CRA, sta RASTER, sta $d800,x for colour RAM without a name, not an offset of the data label at $d000), a platform name in a knowledge operand expression stays as written and becomes a constant in constants.asm, and the RAM keeps its data label without a platform-name label, because a game that copies sprites under the I/O area got every register access written as region+offset; a user or LLM name at the address still wins
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: c64-assembler: an include folder can be anywhere in the project folder, for example build src boot.asm --include ../build for a file that you generated next to the source root: the script stages only the source root and the include folders from the lowest folder that holds them, ACME runs in the source root inside that tree, a diagnostic in such a folder names the file from the source root (../build/tables.asm), and a folder outside the project is refused by name; before, a path with .. was refused and the project folder had to be the source root, which staged the whole project
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: c64-provenance: match keeps the overlapping copies of a routine and names a routine with several copies only at the copy that has the shift of its nearest library neighbours that occur once, or at no copy with an ambiguous reason for each, because the lowest copy was often the wrong one; a $xxxx address in a library comment inside the routine moves by the shift of the match, and a written comment with an address outside the routine is in batch.check for the agent to examine
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: c64-testing: a run file and a scenario name a missing or wrong field with its form (name is a non-empty string, start is a program, a program with load or a snapshot, original and rebuild have program and symbols) and refuse a key that they do not have with the list of their keys, and the run help, SKILL.md and the format reference give the required and optional fields of a run file, because a run file without name failed with "needs a name" and the help did not tell that name is required
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: c64-source: the export rewrite of a scenario gives each side only program and symbols, because a scenario now refuses any other key in original and rebuild and a copied videoStandard made the rewritten scenario fail
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: c64-source: when the check of loader.prg cannot run (the emulator is not available, or another refusal), generate --loader removes the loader.prg that it wrote and gives the normal result with loader.verified false and the reason, and a run without --loader that keeps a loader.asm of another knowledge revision gives staleLoader with the files and a generate --loader nextAction, because an unchecked or stale loader.prg looked like a checked one and a failed check lost the list of written files
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: An overdue binary-monitor request whose answer never comes no longer caps every later request at the short overdue time limit: VICE answers in order, so the answer to a later request clears each overdue request sent before it, and slow commands such as memmap, hunt, step and snapshot get their full time limit again after VICE goes on
events.author: Henrik Olsson

before.name: Q8 accelerated-emulation qualification
before.notes: Upstream recommends Q8 only above 20 MHz. v1.8.0 reports Turbo6510 64 MHz measurements on public PAL cube scenes: Mode 2 precise/hybrid 23.70/25.05 FPS, Mode 5 27.00/27.45 FPS, and distant-cube Mode 7 standard/fast/fast+LOD 3.10/6.95/11.50 FPS. These are scene-specific emulator measurements, not minima, general guarantees or physical-hardware qualification. The v1.10.2 stable qualification additionally reports Mode 4 stock/turbo results of 0.649958/30.186113 FPS with defaults and 0.749952/38.484510 FPS with arithmetic, camera and visibility experiments; Mode 7 defaults report 0.044442/3.091013 FPS and arithmetic+UV 0.061107/3.703647 FPS. These remain emulator measurements, not physical-hardware or minimum-machine claims.

after.name: Q8 accelerated-emulation qualification
after.notes: Upstream recommends Q8 only above 20 MHz. v1.8.0 reports Turbo6510 64 MHz measurements on public PAL cube scenes: Mode 2 precise/hybrid 23.70/25.05 FPS, Mode 5 27.00/27.45 FPS, and distant-cube Mode 7 standard/fast/fast+LOD 3.10/6.95/11.50 FPS. These are scene-specific emulator measurements, not minima, general guarantees or physical-hardware qualification. The v1.10.2 stable qualification additionally reports Mode 4 stock/turbo results of 0.649958/30.186113 FPS with defaults and 0.749952/38.484510 FPS with arithmetic, camera and visibility experiments; Mode 7 defaults report 0.044442/3.091013 FPS and arithmetic+UV 0.061107/3.703647 FPS. These remain emulator measurements, not physical-hardware or minimum-machine claims.

before.name: Swift64 v0.4.2 Apple Silicon application
before.notes: The universal release was packaged and run to BASIC READY on Apple Silicon. User-supplied BASIC, KERNAL and character ROMs are required; 1541 media/ROM support varies by mode. No CPU-generation or RAM minimum is stated.

before.name: Swift64 v0.4.2 Intel application slice
before.notes: The universal release explicitly includes an Intel binary, but upstream labels it build-verified rather than runtime-tested. User-supplied ROMs are required; no CPU-generation or RAM minimum is stated.

EmuTOS's 6x6 font joins the ST font download (for VDI's small text). before.name: Q8 accelerated-emulation qualification
before.notes: Upstream recommends Q8 only above 20 MHz. v1.8.0 reports Turbo6510 64 MHz measurements on public PAL cube scenes: Mode 2 precise/hybrid 23.70/25.05 FPS, Mode 5 27.00/27.45 FPS, and distant-cube Mode 7 standard/fast/fast+LOD 3.10/6.95/11.50 FPS. These are scene-specific emulator measurements, not minima, general guarantees or physical-hardware qualification. The v1.10.2 stable qualification additionally reports Mode 4 stock/turbo results of 0.649958/30.186113 FPS with defaults and 0.749952/38.484510 FPS with arithmetic, camera and visibility experiments; Mode 7 defaults report 0.044442/3.091013 FPS and arithmetic+UV 0.061107/3.703647 FPS. These remain emulator measurements, not physical-hardware or minimum-machine claims.

after.name: Q8 accelerated-emulation qualification
after.notes: Upstream recommends Q8 only above 20 MHz. v1.8.0 reports Turbo6510 64 MHz measurements on public PAL cube scenes: Mode 2 precise/hybrid 23.70/25.05 FPS, Mode 5 27.00/27.45 FPS, and distant-cube Mode 7 standard/fast/fast+LOD 3.10/6.95/11.50 FPS. These are scene-specific emulator measurements, not minima, general guarantees or physical-hardware qualification. The v1.10.2 stable qualification additionally reports Mode 4 stock/turbo results of 0.649958/30.186113 FPS with defaults and 0.749952/38.484510 FPS with arithmetic, camera and visibility experiments; Mode 7 defaults report 0.044442/3.091013 FPS and arithmetic+UV 0.061107/3.703647 FPS. These remain emulator measurements, not physical-hardware or minimum-machine claims.

evidence.excerpt: AmigaOS 3.0 or later; 68020 minimum, no FPU required; AGA chipset, or a graphics card (RTG / Picasso96).

after.name: Native AmigaOS build
after.notes: README states 68020 minimum with no FPU, AGA or RTG graphics, and enough memory for about 20 MB of sprite graphics plus sound samples. That working-set description is not treated as an exact total-RAM minimum; 68060 is recommended for AGA and a fast 68040 for RTG. v0.8.2 recommends 320x240 on slower machines, and Shell launches require the documented 2 MB stack that the icon already supplies.

events.title: Files for other editors: Save as now ends with "For other editors: ..." formats for the page types they fit. iCEDraw .idf, ArtWorx .adf and TundraDraw .tnd are written as well as read (written the way ansilove and IcyDraw read them: character 1 always as a run, counts up to 255, both Tundra colours on the first cell, characters 1-6 inside a colour command, SAUCE without comment lines); IcyDraw .icy (a PNG with icYD records; read in version 1, zstd-packed or not, and the older base64 version 0, layers put together) and REXPaint .xp are read and written; Playscii .psci keeps every frame with its hold, mapped to Playscii's own charsets and palettes (their glyph order found by comparing their pictures with the ROM fonts); Marq's PETSCII editor gets .pet, .bas and .s, and Petmate its JSON export. The ones that open again become the page's file, so Save writes the same format (before, Ctrl+S on an opened .idf wrote XBin bytes into it), and their SAUCE title and author are kept. Checked against ansilove (identical pictures), IcyDraw 0.6's engine and Playscii's own loader (both run in a sandbox without network), and against files IcyDraw wrote (testdata/icydraw); new readers fuzzed. The zstd decoder is klauspost/compress (BSD). Help, README (Files for other editors, Licences) and HANDOFF.

Below Large a draw order puts down short runs of cells together (3 at Medium, 8 at Small, so Small costs about a tenth more than the plain file), Fade in draws fewer passes, and the frame effects take fewer frames held longer (about as long in all), with less glyph churn, shorter trails, shorter flights and fewer shade and glint steps. The level is kept with the page's draw order (detail). The cost of an order is worked out by what Save writes: the file's size, the bytes the caller gets, the board's pauses, the time at a speed, and a weight (light, medium or heavy by bytes per cell that shows something). events.title: Moebius files open as Moebius shows them, and keys like Moebius, PabloDraw, TheDraw or ACiDDraw. A corpus of 69 files written by Moebius's own save code (tools/moebius/gen.js runs its libtextmode from a separate checkout) is checked cell for cell against Moebius's own reader (testdata/moebius, moebius_test.go), and CharEdit's saves read back in Moebius as the same page (tools/moebius/check.js). Fixed on the way: SAUCE widths from 1 column; the SAUCE height when the record has the aspect-ratio bits (Moebius writes nothing for empty rows at the end); characters 0, 7, 8 and 9 are glyphs in files with SAUCE and saved as they were (real files with NULs and tabs as art now line up); SAUCE text and comments in UTF-8 read and written back; an XBin's SAUCE read and written; a SAUCE font name CharEdit lacks kept, shown in the CP437 font of its size; Moebius's UTF-8 export (VT wrap, its width, 256-colour codes); a PC file full of ESC [ is not taken for ATASCII. 9-pixel letter spacing from the SAUCE flag is drawn (line characters reach the ninth column) and toggled with Alt+9; letter spacing and aspect bits are kept on save. Settings > Keys like writes a preset line into the keys file (the old file kept as keys.bak, the user's own lines still win); every preset is clash-free (tests). Help, README (Coming from Moebius, PabloDraw, TheDraw or ACiDDraw), HANDOFF and roadmap. The big check: 29 issues, as before.

events.title: Animate a folder, for sysops: every screen of a folder animated for the board at once (Alt+Shift+J, a button in the Open requester, or charedit --animate on the command line). One effect for all, or a different one for each file from all or the ticked ones, never the same twice in a row, Reverse and Flip at random, from a seed that is shown and can be typed so a run repeats exactly. The pace, the board and copies as in Animate. N versions of each screen are named the way the board picks one at random (Ami-Express 001.NAME.TXT with ~<n>SR_ in NAME.TXT, Mystic name.an1 to .an8, Synchronet name1.ans for a wildcard menu; the others numbered). The files go to a new folder with their names; the originals are never touched unless Replace is ticked, and then each keeps a .bak. A progress bar with Cancel, then a report of each file, its effect and seed, the sizes and what was skipped and why, saved as animate-report.txt. Tests read every written file back through each board's model to exactly the original picture. Help, README, HANDOFF and roadmap.

events.title: Own fonts and character sets (roadmap 2.3): a page takes a font from a file (PC raw .fnt/.f08/.f14/.f16, PSF1/PSF2, an XBin's font, C64/VIC/PET .64c and .bin sets, Atari .fnt, Spectrum 768-byte sets and UDGs), named after the file; Load a font... (Ctrl+Shift+L) or a dropped font file, which asks first. XBin and Petmate (customFonts, read and written) keep the font inside; other formats have CharEdit remember it per file (prefs art_fonts, a copy in the data folder's fonts/) and say so in the status line; autosaves keep it too. Built-in PC fonts from VileR's pack: EGA 8x14, VGA 8x8 (80x50), CP850 and CP866, drawn from the pack's bitmap fonts by tools/pcfonts.py (EGA and VGA 8x8 byte for byte DOSBox's ROM tables); 14-row cells; SAUCE font names chosen on opening and written on saving

before.name: Q8 accelerated-emulation qualification
before.notes: Upstream recommends Q8 only above 20 MHz. v1.8.0 reports Turbo6510 64 MHz measurements on public PAL cube scenes: Mode 2 precise/hybrid 23.70/25.05 FPS, Mode 5 27.00/27.45 FPS, and distant-cube Mode 7 standard/fast/fast+LOD 3.10/6.95/11.50 FPS. These are scene-specific emulator measurements, not minima, general guarantees or physical-hardware qualification.

after.name: Q8 accelerated-emulation qualification
after.notes: Upstream recommends Q8 only above 20 MHz. v1.8.0 reports Turbo6510 64 MHz measurements on public PAL cube scenes: Mode 2 precise/hybrid 23.70/25.05 FPS, Mode 5 27.00/27.45 FPS, and distant-cube Mode 7 standard/fast/fast+LOD 3.10/6.95/11.50 FPS. These are scene-specific emulator measurements, not minima, general guarantees or physical-hardware qualification. The v1.10.2 stable qualification additionally reports Mode 4 stock/turbo results of 0.649958/30.186113 FPS with defaults and 0.749952/38.484510 FPS with arithmetic, camera and visibility experiments; Mode 7 defaults report 0.044442/3.091013 FPS and arithmetic+UV 0.061107/3.703647 FPS. These remain emulator measurements, not physical-hardware or minimum-machine claims.

change_details.after: v1.10.2 stable source SDK released; optional Q8 experiments remain emulator-qualified and physical hardware remains untested

before.name: A1200 release
before.notes: Author specifies Amiga 1200 or WinUAE configured as one. Fast RAM recommended but not required for release; debug executable requires fast RAM. Three original game disks required.

after.name: A1200 release
after.notes: Author specifies Amiga 1200 or WinUAE configured as one: 68020, AGA, Kickstart 3.x and 2 MiB chip RAM. Fast RAM is recommended but not required for release; debug requires fast RAM. Three original game disks are required. Network play additionally needs bsdsocket.library from WinUAE or an Amiga TCP/IP stack.

change_details.before: Upstream-reported playable A1200 reconstruction; original disks required; public-build proof documented.
change_details.after: v0.2.0 Amiga HD release; playable A1200 reconstruction with local/network co-op; Windows SDL port in progress

events.title: Project metadata updated

before.name: MEGA65 R6 (upstream-tested beta)
before.notes: README explicitly reports 0.4.7 beta tested on a real R6. Requires the board’s SDRAM, SD card, tos.img and user media. R4/R5 projects are advertised but explicitly untested; R3/R3A are unsupported. No 45GS02 requirement or guest ST-RAM size is used as a host CPU/RAM minimum.

after.name: MegaST v1.0 on MEGA65 R6
after.notes: Primary README reports stable real-hardware R6 operation with floppy/hard-disk images, TOS 1.04, named games and additional tester-reported TOS/game configurations. Requires an SD card, tos.img and user media. No 45GS02 requirement or guest ST-RAM size is treated as a host CPU/RAM minimum.

after.name: MegaST v1.0 on MEGA65 R3/R3A
after.notes: The dedicated R3/R3A core keeps 512 KiB of guest ST RAM in FPGA block RAM because HyperRAM is too slow for cycle-exact timing. Upstream reports R3A operation including hard-disk images. Viking and STEroids modes are unavailable. The 512 KiB value is guest configuration, not host minimum RAM.

change_details.before: 0.4.7 beta; author-tested on MEGA65 R6, further hardware modes untested
change_details.after: v1.0 stable; upstream-tested on MEGA65 R6 and R3A; R4/R5 untested

before.name: Fractalus and Void Trader: selected classic AGA builds
before.notes: Both selected builds use -m68020, explicit AGA 320x256x8bpp and v39 OS libraries. No minimum RAM or measured performance threshold is established. 64 KiB stack requests are not RAM minima.

before.name: Fractalus and Void Trader: PPC OS4 variants
before.notes: ARCH=ppc selects -mcpu=440 and newlib with sam460ex/QEMU intent. The PPC variants use silent audio stubs; Fractalus uses graphics.library fallback rendering. Pacing/freezing limitations are author-reported. This does not cover Dot Chase or the whole collection; exact CPU/RAM minimum remains unverified.
